Redwood proposed MAP (dates are target windows):
- Apr 3–6: Technical kickoff (test accounts, performance targets, KV/caching config) — Owner: Soojin (Redwood SE)
- Apr 7–10: Security evidence handoff (SOC2 artifact set + RFI answers) — Owner: Security (cc’d via portal) — deliverable: security bundle
- Apr 11–13: Private Offer creation & acceptance (AWS private offer draft + vendor acceptance) — Owner: Karthik (Marketplace Ops)
- Apr 14–17: Legal redline + DocuSign signature routing — Owner: Redwood Legal (liaison: Soojin)
- Apr 18–20: Procurement PO issuance and vendor portal upload — Owner: CloudBasket Procurement
- Apr 21–30: Billing onboarding (invoice routing confirmation, billing contact, SaaS metering) — Owner: Laura (Finance)

Notes on billing path options (we’ll confirm with Laura):
A) Marketplace-billed: AWS issues monthly invoice to CloudBasket; Redwood reconciles via the accepted private offer. This is common for AWS Private Offers and preserves marketplace-led payments.
B) Direct-billed: Redwood issues a monthly invoice directly to CloudBasket (requires finance onboarding and a billing contract).

I will prepare a one-page MAP PDF and upload RFI answers. Karthik, can you confirm the private offer cadence and whether the AWS_Private_Offer_Template is sufficient for CloudBasket’s procurement? Laura, any blockers on establishing direct-billing if they prefer that route?

Thanks — I’ll send an updated MAP doc by EOD.

— Soojin

Thanks for the ping — quick clarifications on AWS private offer flow and timings:

- AWS Private Offer steps: Redwood uploads the commercial terms and private offer template to AWS; CloudBasket creates a commitment on their side and sends a signed PO to AWS/Redwood. AWS will then accept the offer and start the marketplace billing linkage.
- Expected lead time: once the private offer is submitted, acceptance typically takes 48–72 hours if there are no commercial exceptions.
- Billing mechanics we typically see:
  * Marketplace billing: CloudBasket receives an AWS marketplace invoice monthly; that invoice covers charges rendered by the private offer. CloudBasket’s finance team pays AWS. Redwood receives payout per marketplace settlement schedule.
  * Direct billing: possible but requires a billing agreement with Redwood and typically delays go-live by 5–7 business days due to credit checks and contract setup.

For CloudBasket’s timeline (legal upload by Apr 20), we can prioritize the private offer route to keep billing through the marketplace and avoid direct-billing setup friction. I’ve attached the AWS_Private_Offer_Template.pdf for procurement — it contains the fields procurement will need to include.

I’ll be the internal owner for creating the private offer and shepherding it through the marketplace. Soojin, please confirm the commercial terms (term length, committed spend) and I’ll draft the offer tonight.

— Karthik
Marketplace Ops, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: AWS_Private_Offer_Template.pdf)

- Billing contact (name + email) and billing PO number format they will use;
- Any tax-exempt certificates (if applicable) uploaded to vendor portal;
- Confirmation on whether they will remit on AWS invoice or require Redwood to send a separate invoice (this changes revenue recognition timing).

If they do later opt for direct-billing, please note Redwood requires a 30-day net payment term standard and a credit review. For the MAP we should flag the billing owner and expected invoice cadence.

Laura Bennett
